text: Okay, so this is the 15th level of this game, and I'm making these levels in chronological order. So I started with level one, then level two, then level three, etc, etc. And up until level 14, which was the last level, which you may have played, depending on if you came from the main menu or if you played through the entire thing, I was just kind of sitting in my room, chipping away, adding more systems and content to this project, and not really showing it to anyone. I might have shown an occasional, like, screen recording to a friend of something, but no one had really played through the game. And then I decided that I wanted this to exist in some way out in the world, not just, like, on my hard drive, so I bundled everything into a, like, 20-minute demo that I uploaded. And of course, no one, like, not many people play this, but I was able to force a few friends to try to play through the whole thing. Now, the majority of these friends weren't even able to complete the game, because I had accidentally, like, always-happens-made-it-too-difficult, kind of blind to the challenge of navigating the world that I myself had created. But receiving this feedback from them, like, even if it was painful to feel like I had pushed a piece of software into their hands, forced them to use it, and forced them to feel this immense frustration, it also did, in a way, inspire me to keep making changes to the game. And I think this is not only because it gave me a list of, like, actionable items that I could fix inside of the game, but also because suddenly the game had a receiver. There was someone that I could send it out to that would actually play it, and if they were able- if I was able to fix these issues, if they were able to play through the levels, it would also mean that they would receive these messages that I am recording. I've kind of thought about this project as my own little baby, my creative pursuit, the place where I can take solely what is inside of my mind, my ideas and my thoughts, and push it into a thing that becomes a result of whatever is in here, and release that into the world. But now I'm starting to question the meaning of that whole idea, because perhaps what is more interesting than pushing my own thoughts and ideas into the world is to create something that becomes a space for conversation. Like, in each of these levels, I'm just throwing my own polished thoughts and ideas right onto the canvas that is this game, and it's not really like I have anything meaningful to say, I don't really have a point, I just have thoughts and questions that I'm curious about, and what I really am looking for, or maybe what I should be looking for, isn't someone that wants to listen to what I have to say, but rather someone that wants to participate in creating the thoughts themselves. So from now on, I'm not going to just sit here and chip away, adding more and more content into this game by myself. Instead, with each level that I create, I'm going to make a build, share it, and have at least one person, probably a friend, play it and give me their thoughts on what it is that they're playing. And the point of this is not so that I can iterate and make the game better and better, but rather to have this whole thing become a vessel for having conversations with people. So however you are out there, whoever it is that is currently playing this level on the other end, I genuinely want to talk to you, I want to know what you think, because that matters as much as what I think. As a starting point, I will end this level by letting you send whatever it is that is currently floating around in your head right to me in the form of a text.
